items.title: BNP Paribas Cardif to acquire Warburg’s 26% in IndiaFirst Life
items.description: BNP Paribas Cardif will re-enter India's life insurance market soon.  The French insurer is acquiring Warburg Pincus' stake in IndiaFirst Life.  This transaction values the Bank of Baroda-controlled insurer at approximately ten thousand crore rupees.  Bank of Baroda will retain its controlling interest and management control.  BNP Paribas Cardif will hold twenty-six percent of the insurer's shares.

items.title: Sebi fines Axis MF former dealer for front-running
items.description: Sebi imposed penalties totaling ₹7.5 crore on Viresh Joshi and 20 others.  The former Axis Mutual Fund chief dealer orchestrated a front-running scheme.  He misused confidential information to generate illegal gains for himself.  Joshi and Dubai-based trader Prijesh Kurani received seven-year market bans.  The regulator found substantial illegal gains and significant market abuse.

items.title: Nifty closes below key 23,800 level on Gulf war ripples
items.description: Indian equities experienced a decline on Friday, influenced by rising crude oil prices. The depreciation of the Indian rupee also contributed to investor apprehension during the trading session. Major indices partially recovered from earlier lows, but the Nifty closed below a key support level. This closing position suggests a potential for further downward movement in the market.

items.title: Wall Street Week Ahead: US stocks face tests from Fed decision, tech-led earnings deluge
items.description: Investors await the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision and corporate earnings reports.  Technology giants and artificial intelligence companies will release their quarterly results.  Rising oil prices and inflation concerns add complexity to the economic outlook.  The market remains sensitive to any signs of economic imperfection and policy shifts.  Future interest rate movements will significantly influence investor sentiment and stock valuations.

items.title: Stock picks of the week: 6 stocks with consistent score improvement and upside potential of up to 26%
items.description: The US-Iran war continues to create uncertainty for markets across the globe. But more so in India, due to the high correlation between energy costs and inflation and, subsequently, consumption. Adding to the uncertainty, at least in some sectors, is the renewal of the tariff war. Our selected stocks for today depict a strong upward trajectory in their overall average score which is based on five key pillars: Earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum. This implies that there has been a significant improvement in their market outlook in the given time frame.
